title: Reader-value contract
description: The defined human benefit an article promises before drafting and must deliver before it ships. It lives in a fenced block under '## Reader Value Contract' in any markdown file, or in a standalone .toml or .json file. The sales CTA NEVER counts as reader value. Procedural fields are required only for procedural types: history and commentary aren't forced into steps. Generalised from a blog workspace's contract: the field set is unchanged; the descriptions no longer name particular sites.

type.description: Practical guides favour task/decision/self_check; technical posts favour implementation/debugging_path; history favours evidence_trail/historical_interpretation.

problem.description: The reader's problem or question, in their words.

decision.description: The decision the article helps the reader make (required for type=decision).

promised_outcome.description: What the reader has/knows/can do after reading. Never a CTA.

effort.description: Honest effort/time estimate. If stated as a specific figure it is a claim — ledger it where material.

success_signal.description: How the reader knows it worked / expected output.

stop_condition.description: When to stop, skip, or seek help.

original_value.description: The author's real, specific contribution, not 'unique perspective'.

evidence_trail.description: The sources, places or questions the piece equips the reader to explore.

cta_excluded_confirmed.description: Assertion that the promised outcome and value calculation exclude every sales CTA.
